q-108578.name: Question 1
q-108578.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/448ae88055ea0da5dd44fb3db608b5ac71dbd3709c88edd41440c15124d74eae.png)

Which of the graphs above correspond to an invertible function?
q-108578.worked_solution:
A function is invertible if and only if it's a one-to-one function. To determine which of the functions are one-to-one, we use the horizontal line test.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/e582f5233163be3a094ac575ba0cf2a37b417038be8894a12717ca31d401e4d6.png)

From the above, we see that:

- For graphs I, III, and IV, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line. Therefore, graphs I, III, and IV show one-to-one functions. As a result, those functions are invertible.

- For graph II, some horizontal lines intersect the curve more than once. So, this is not a one-to-one function. As a result, it is not invertible.

q-36011.name: Question 3
q-36011.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/b02c2e94e144935f0ff96846cd51b5a969fa8f884a7ca1d09abb231b7c945232.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible? 

I. $x\in (-4,-2)$

II. $x\in [-2,3]$

III. $x\in [-3,3]$
q-36011.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.  

- The given function is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-4,-2)$ and $x\in [-2,3].$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/53fe88780b2ccb7522d2f1baa711162ec99300c2a2d4da29bba9ca532026cd07.png)

- The given function is **not** invertible on  the interval $x\in [-3,3]$  because some lines will  intersect the curve at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/63cee4fc05ab17a8e69d9bfae578fa83c24d73e4677065a54a33a25e0871e718.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

Determine the largest domain on which the function $f(x)$ (shown above) is invertible.
q-36939.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain of our function is $x\in [-4,4].$ 

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ does not pass the horizontal line test on the interval $x\in (-1,1).$ In this case, the horizontal line $y=1$ intersects the graph at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/d295d104bd8340a8701327e19103bfa8fd12622f1500c405411d2afd8bd47801.png)

- Among the given options, the largest domain on which the function $f(x)$ is invertible is $x\in [-4,-1)\cup [0,4].$ On this domain, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/a74a9a3f1fe52a7c841c763ccffb51faa922fdaec56825ef1000b5becc3534fe.png)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is $x\in [-4,-1)\cup [0,4].$

q-36939.html:
Question 4
?

Determine the largest domain on which the function f(x) (shown above) is invertible.

a
x∈[0,4]
b
x∈[−4,4]
c
x∈[−4,−1)∪[0,4]
d
x∈[−4,−1]
e
x∈[−1,4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the domain of our function is x∈[−4,4].

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

  • The function f(x) does not pass the horizontal line test on the interval x∈(−1,1). In this case, the horizontal line y=1 intersects the graph at more than one point.
  • Among the given options, the largest domain on which the function f(x) is invertible is x∈[−4,−1)∪[0,4]. On this domain, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

Therefore, the correct answer is x∈[−4,−1)∪[0,4].

q-36010.name: Question 5
q-36010.problem:
Given that $f(x)=|x-2|+1,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

I. $x\in (-\infty ,1]$

II. $x\in (1,\infty )$

III. $x\in (2,4]$
q-36010.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=|x-2|+1$ can be obtained in the following way:

1\. Take the curve $y=|x|.$

2\. Translate it by $2$ units to the right,  to get $y=|x-2|.$

3\. Finally, translate $y=|x-2|$ by $1$ unit up to get $f(x)=|x-2|+1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/ceab1637313ae53869cc1e59f6a56ad6cb920a83dffba482558b696188df0d36.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-\infty ,1]$ and $x\in (2,4].$ On these intervals, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/a47169838785b6f4ac78253252bcedc3c2cb752a655feac9945e20dd40563b4f.png)

  

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (1,\infty ).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14229037/assets/14ed35294e1179ffd9efaf87fa8ac1eb99853a7da344e462c2cb0dda74c3b78f.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
